text:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: GraniteHealth (dedicated pool: gp-d-7) tail latency > 2.5s over 5m. 90th=1.1s 99th=2.8s. Auto-shed triggered for some routes. Paging ops-oncall.
Alex W: seeing spikes on /generate and some short-seq requests getting oversized batches that blow past latency SLO. Tenant is pinned to bespoke scheduler.
Jamie S: confirmed. Metrics: qps ~480, p95 token latency 850ms, p99 token latency 2.7s. Pool utilization 92%.
Maria C: GraniteHealth is on Dedicated (VPC) with custom max_batch_tokens=4096 and aggressive coalescing. They're mostly short prompts (<=64 tokens) but bursty.
Lu P: could be packing inefficiency: long max_batch_tokens lets scheduler wait to fill large batches when bursts are uneven. Suggest temporary tweak -> lower max_batch_tokens and enable tail-preemption.
Alex W: Agreed. Proposal: patch tenant scheduler to max_batch_tokens=1024, packet_timeout_ms=35 -> 15ms for that tenant, and set tail_preemption=true. This should drop queueing delay.
Dari N: +1. Also add a per-tenant queue_capacity cap to avoid impacting others: tenant_queue_limit=150 concurrent in-queue requests.
Jamie S: prepping patch. Applying via infra-configs service. Command: 
```
curl -X PATCH "https://infra-config.internal/v1/tenants/granite/scheduler" -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRATOKEN" -d '{"max_batch_tokens":1024,"packet_timeout_ms":15,"tail_preemption":true,"tenant_queue_limit":150}'
```
Alex W: hit it. Response 200. Rolling config to gp-d-7 shards (3/3).
incident-bot: change deployed to gp-d-7 (rollout id r-77823). Observability: collecting 5m post-change window.
Maria C: watching metrics — within 60s p99 token latency dropped from 2.7s -> 1.1s, p95 -> 420ms. Throughput steady.
Lu P: good sign. Any customer errors?
Jamie S: logs show a few 429s during the config switch (tenants queue limit enforced). Not customer-visible errors in last 2m. I pushed a temporary allowlist for admin routes.
Dari N: Open question: does this change degrade cost-per-token? Might increase number of batches. We'll revert after cool-down if not needed.
Alex W: I'll reach out to SE owning GraniteHealth — brief them and offer increased burst capacity if they want throughput vs latency tradeoff.
Maria C: Also create a short-term automated rollback if p99 rises above 2s again for 3 consecutive 1m windows. Jamie can you create the alert?
Jamie S: On it. Alert created: granite.scheduler.tuning.rollback (auto-rollback annotation).
incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff in 1h. Current status: mitigation applied, latency improved, low 429 noise.
Lu P: I'll take overnight watch. Documented the knobs in the incident runbook and added links to the rollout id and curl command.
Dari N: For the postmortem, we should capture: workload shape (short + bursty), risk of large max_batch_tokens with low packet timeout, and suggestion: provide tenant-specific workload profile to avoid blanket allocator knob settings.
Alex W: Also add a new dashboard tile: per-tenant avg tokens-per-request + inter-arrival distribution. That would've flagged this earlier.
Jamie S: handoff to Lu P — I've annotated the thread with runbook step ids and the rollback alert.
Lu P: ack, taking over. I'll notify GraniteHealth SE in case they see any UX blips.
Maria C: final note: consider a safe-mode that, when a dedicated pool exceeds 90% util and tail-latency > 2s, automatically applies conservative cap (max_batch_tokens=1024) for 15m while paging. Could stop future manual scrubs.
Alex W: +1. Filing follow-up issue in infra-config backlog.
incident-bot: Thread closed for now — mitigation succeeded. Re-open if p99 > 2s.
Lu P: logging closure for handoff: monitoring until 0600 UTC, then re-evaluate.
